searchDocs.title: Cryo
searchDocs.content: Cryo A collection of methods for working with immutable data in a functional way. Operations return new tables rather than mutating their inputs. The library is split into two namespaces: Cryo.Dictionary — operations on string-keyed tables. Cryo.List — operations on array-like tables. Cryo.None is a sentinel that, when passed as a value to dictionary merges, removes the corresponding key from the result.

searchDocs.title: doCleanup​
searchDocs.content: </> doCleanup.doCleanup( ...: unknown-- Tasks to clean up. ) → () Cleans up every task passed as an argument. A task can be any of: an Instance - will be destroyed an RBXScriptConnection - will be disconnected a function - will be run a table with a destroy or Destroy method - will be called an array - each item is cleaned up in reverse order, so tasks run opposite to their construction order, then removed from the array Unrecognised values are ignored.

searchDocs.title: Connect​
searchDocs.content: </> type Connect = (callback: (Args...) → ()) → () → () Registers a listener and returns a function that disconnects it.

searchDocs.title: Event​
searchDocs.content: </> Event.Event() → ( Connect<Args...>,-- Registers a listener; returns its disconnect. (Args...) → ()-- Fires the event to every current listener. ) Creates an event and returns its connect and fire halves. Listeners run on their own threads via task.spawn, so a yielding or erroring listener never blocks the firer or the other listeners.

searchDocs.title: FinallyTask​
searchDocs.content: </> FinallyTask.FinallyTask( taskExec: ( callback, scope, Args... ) → thread,-- Scheduler used to start the callback, e.g. task.spawn. callback: ( scope: {unknown}, Args... ) → (),-- Work to run; receives the cleanup scope first. ...: Args...-- Extra arguments forwarded to the callback. ) → () → ()-- Destructor: cancels the thread (if still running) and cleans up the scope. Safe to call more than once. Spawns callback via taskExec (typically task.spawn or task.defer), passing it a fresh cleanup scope followed by the extra arguments. The callback registers its cleanup tasks into that scope; if it errors, the scope is passed to doCleanup before the error propagates. local stop = FinallyTask(task.spawn, function(scope) table.insert(scope, workspace.ChildAdded:Connect(print)) while true do task.wait(1) end end) -- later: cancels the thread and runs the scope's cleanup stop()

searchDocs.title: selectNearestSize​
searchDocs.content: </> IconRamp.selectNearestSize( ramp: IconRamp, targetSize: number-- Size the icon will be displayed at, in pixels. ) → Icon? Returns the smallest icon in the ramp that is at least targetSize pixels, so icons are only ever downscaled, never blurred upward. Falls back to the largest icon when the ramp has nothing big enough; returns nil only for an empty ramp. ramp itself is left unsorted.

searchDocs.title: action​
searchDocs.content: </> input.action( v: Action-- An action descriptor with a type discriminator. ) → ActionTypes Reconciles an action descriptor into an InputAction instance and returns it augmented with the ActionFunctions API (is_pressed, is_released, is_changed, get_state, plus pressed, released, and state_changed signals). The return type is narrowed by the type field on the descriptor: "bool" → ActionBool, "1d" → Action1D, etc.

searchDocs.title: clear_state​
searchDocs.content: </> input.clear_state() → () Clears the per-frame transient state (is_pressed, is_released, is_changed flags) for every action. Call this once per frame before polling so each press/release/state-change is observed exactly once.

searchDocs.title: capture_input​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> input.capture_input() → { bind: Enum.KeyCode, modifier1: Enum.KeyCode, modifier2: Enum.KeyCode } Yields until the user produces input, then returns a table containing the primary KeyCode along with up to two modifier keys held during the press. Mouse buttons and touch are translated to their KeyCode equivalents.

searchDocs.title: track​
searchDocs.content: </> Leader.track( scope: {unknown},-- Cleanup scope (see doCleanup) owning the tracker's connections and task. interposer: InterposerApi-- A logged-on Interposer session to elect over. ) → LeaderApi

interface LeaderApi { leader: () → Peer?-- Current leader, or nil while undecided. selfIsLeader: () → boolean?-- Whether this peer leads; nil while undecided. onLeaderChanged: Connect<Peer?>-- Fires whenever a different leader takes over. }  Joins the election and starts tracking leadership. The search runs on a background task registered into scope; cleaning up the scope stops tracking and, if this peer is the leader, hands leadership over first.

searchDocs.title: yield​
searchDocs.content: </> PushPull.yield() → ( (Values...) → (),-- push: enqueues a value and wakes a waiting puller. () → Values...-- pull: dequeues the next value, yielding while the queue is empty. ) Creates a queue whose pull yields the calling coroutine until a value is pushed. Values are delivered first-in first-out and each is consumed once. Useful as a wake-up channel inside long-running loops.

searchDocs.title: maybe​
searchDocs.content: </> PushPull.maybe() → ( (Value) → (),-- push: enqueues a value. () → Maybe<Value>-- pull: dequeues the next value, or a None when empty. ) Creates a non-blocking queue: pull returns Maybe.some(value) when a value is buffered and Maybe.none when the queue is empty, never yielding.

searchDocs.title: sortingBy​
searchDocs.content: </> sortingBy.sortingBy( extract: (T) → {number | string}-- Maps a value to its sort keys, most significant first. ) → ( T, T ) → boolean-- Comparator for table.sort. Returns a comparator that orders two values by comparing their extracted keys pairwise: the first unequal key decides. Every call of extract must return the same number of keys, and mixing types at the same position will error inside table.sort. table.sort(items, sortingBy(function(item) return { item.category, item.price } end))

searchDocs.title: Categories​
searchDocs.content: The packages are split into two top-level groups:  Modules: runtime libraries for Roblox experiences, such as immutable data, player utilities, type validation, and decompression.Plugin libraries: helpers built for Roblox Studio plugins.  The API tab in the navigation bar has the full list, or jump straight to a package via its sidebar entry.

searchDocs.title: Installing​
searchDocs.content: Add the packages you need to your wally.toml:  [dependencies] Cryo = "morgann1/cryo@1.1.1" SimpleLogger = "morgann1/simple-logger@0.1.2"   Then run wally install to fetch them into your project.

searchDocs.title: gunzip​
searchDocs.content: </> zzlib.gunzip( str: string-- Gzip-compressed input. ) → string-- Decompressed output. Decompresses a gzip-formatted byte string and returns the raw bytes.

searchDocs.title: inflate​
searchDocs.content: </> zzlib.inflate( str: string-- Zlib-compressed input. ) → string-- Decompressed output. Decompresses a zlib-formatted byte string and returns the raw bytes.

searchDocs.title: files​
searchDocs.content: </> zzlib.files( buf: string-- The full ZIP archive bytes. ) → () Returns a stateless iterator over every entry in a ZIP archive. Each iteration yields (name, offset, size, packed, crc) for one file header. Use zzlib.unzip to extract a specific entry.

searchDocs.title: unzip​
searchDocs.content: </> zzlib.unzip( buf: string,-- The full ZIP archive bytes. arg1: string | number,-- Filename to extract, or raw offset. arg2: number?-- Expected CRC when arg1 is a numeric offset. ) → string-- Decompressed file contents. Extracts a single file from a ZIP archive. When arg1 is a string, it's treated as the filename to extract; the function searches the archive and returns the decompressed bytes, or errors if the file isn't present. When arg1 is a number, it's treated as a raw offset into buf and arg2 is the expected CRC.

searchDocs.title: Def​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Def { ExpectsType: string-- Human-readable name of the type, used in errors. NotOfTypeError: string-- Base error message for failed casts. Matches: ( self: Def, x: unknown ) → boolean-- Whether x fits, without converting. Cast: ( self: Def, x: unknown ) → Maybe<unknown>-- Converts x, or a None explaining the mismatch. }

searchDocs.title: Unknown​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Unknown: Def Matches anything; casts pass values through unchanged. Its opposite isty.Never, which matches nothing.

searchDocs.title: Number​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Number: Def typeof-based defs for the primitive types: ty.Number, ty.Boolean, ty.String, ty.Thread, ty.Table and ty.Function.

searchDocs.title: True​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.True: Def Literal defs for the three singleton values: ty.True, ty.False and ty.Nil.

searchDocs.title: IntoDefault​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.IntoDefault( innerDef: Def, defaultValue: any-- Substituted when the input is nil. ) → Def Casts nil to defaultValue; any other value goes through the inner def. Use for optional fields that should come out filled in.

searchDocs.title: Tuple​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Tuple( options: {exhaustive: boolean}, tuple: {Def}-- Def per position. ) → Def The numeric-keyed counterpart of Struct: each position has its own def. Same missing-field and exhaustive semantics.

searchDocs.title: Struct​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Struct( options: {exhaustive: boolean}, object: {[string]: Def}-- Field name to the def its value must satisfy. ) → Def Matches string-keyed tables field-by-field. Casting rebuilds the table from the declared fields, so a missing field fails unless its def isOptional or IntoDefault. With exhaustive = true, keys outside the declaration reject the cast; otherwise they are silently dropped.

searchDocs.title: CastOrError​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.CastOrError( def: Def, x: unknown ) → unknown-- The cast value. Casts x through the def and returns the converted value directly, erroring with the cast's reason chain instead of returning a Maybe. The assertion-style entry point at trust boundaries.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	DescriptionCould not cast	When `x` does not fit the def.

searchDocs.title: IntoTagged​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.IntoTagged( innerDef: Def, tag: unknown-- Discriminant stored under __tag. ) → Def Casts through the inner def, then stamps the result with a __tag field for discriminated unions. Table results are cloned before tagging; other values are wrapped as { value = result, __tag = tag }.

searchDocs.title: Just​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Just( literal: unknown,-- The only accepted value. type: string?-- Display name; defaults to tostring(literal). ) → Def Matches exactly one value, compared with rawequal. Chain with Or for string-literal unions: ty.Just("light"):Or(ty.Just("dark")).

searchDocs.title: MapOf​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.MapOf( keys: Def, values: Def ) → Def Matches dictionaries where every key fits keys and every value fits values. Casting rebuilds the table with both keys and values cast. As a method, the def becomes the key type: IconVariant:MapOf(ty.String).

searchDocs.title: Predicate​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Predicate(predicate: (unknown) → boolean) → Def Builds a def from a boolean function; casting passes matching values through unchanged. The escape hatch for checks the other combinators can't express.

searchDocs.title: Optional​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Optional(innerDef: Def) → Def Also accepts nil, which matches and casts to nil. The runtime equivalent of Luau's T?.

searchDocs.title: Typeof​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Typeof(typeString: string) → Def Matches values whose typeof() equals the given string. Works for Roblox datatypes too: ty.Typeof("Vector2"), ty.Typeof("Instance").

searchDocs.title: IgnoreInvalid​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.IgnoreInvalid(innerDef: Def) → Def Makes a def infallible: values that fit the inner def cast normally, anything else casts to nil instead of failing. Inside Array, this drops invalid elements from the result.

searchDocs.title: Or​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Or( first: Def, last: Def ) → Def Union: matches values fitting either def. Casting tries first and falls back to last, so put the more specific (or more converting) def first.

searchDocs.title: IntoNumber​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.IntoNumber( innerDef: Def, base: number?-- Numeric base for the conversion, as in tonumber. ) → Def-- Casts to a number. Casts through the inner def, then converts the result with tonumber. Fails when the conversion returns nil.

searchDocs.title: Array​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Array( values: Def-- Def each element must satisfy. ) → Def Matches contiguous numeric arrays whose every element fits values. Casting rebuilds the array with each element cast; wrap the element def in IgnoreInvalid to drop failing elements instead of rejecting the whole array.

searchDocs.title: Retype​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Retype(def: Def) → Def Returns the def unchanged; exists purely so call sites can reassert the def's static Luau type. No runtime effect, like Untyped.

searchDocs.title: Untyped​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Untyped(def: Def) → Def Returns the def unchanged; exists purely to erase the def's static Luau type at call sites. No runtime effect, like Retype.

searchDocs.title: IntoString​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.IntoString(innerDef: Def) → Def-- Casts to a string. Casts through the inner def, then converts the result with tostring.

searchDocs.title: And​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.And( first: Def, last: Def ) → Def Intersection: matches values that satisfy both defs. Casting pipes the first def's output into the last, so converting defs compose.

searchDocs.title: Nicknamed​
searchDocs.content: </> ty.Nicknamed( innerDef: Def, newName: string ) → Def Renames a def's ExpectsType so error messages read as your domain name instead of the expanded structural type.

searchDocs.title: span​
searchDocs.content: </> WideLogger.span() → () Open a new span. Set fields on it as the operation progresses, then call :finish() to emit the wide event.

searchDocs.title: withSpan​
searchDocs.content: </> WideLogger.withSpan() → () Open a span, run fn(span), and finish the span automatically. If fn errors, the span is marked failed and the error is rethrown after the event is emitted. Returns whatever fn returned on success.

searchDocs.title: set​
searchDocs.content: </> WideLogger:set() → () Attach a single field to the span. Returns the span for chaining.

searchDocs.title: merge​
searchDocs.content: </> WideLogger:merge() → () Attach a table of fields to the span at once. Existing keys are overwritten. Returns the span for chaining.

searchDocs.title: fail​
searchDocs.content: </> WideLogger:fail() → () Mark the span as failed and attach the given error. The span will be emitted via warn when finished. Returns the span for chaining.

searchDocs.title: finish​
searchDocs.content: </> WideLogger:finish() → () Emit the wide event. Subsequent calls are no-ops. After this, calls toset/merge/fail are also no-ops.
